Welcome
Welcome to Bourton-on-the-Water Primary Academy.
We are a happy, caring school, well established within the local community, where high standards are expected, and pupils are put first. With a well-developed curriculum, we work hard to develop a firm foundation to support your child’s future learning alongside developing each pupil’s individuality and ensuring their well-being.
Children coming to our school bring a variety of experiences and knowledge about the world. We foster this. We have an enthusiastic, happy and well-motivated team whose shared vision is to develop each child and ensure they feel safe, supported and able to reach their potential. We have high expectations of our pupils and have worked hard to create an environment that encompasses our school CARE statement: challenge, amaze, respect and enjoy!
As the Co Headteachers, we are very proud of our school, and proud to lead such a special place. The children, parents, governors and staff work together to make it a very positive community. We are all continually working towards our vision for the school, which is being at the heart of the community; a school where everyone is determined to achieve and share success.
On our website, hopefully you will find all the information you need about our school community. Enjoy reading.
Mrs Kilbey & Mrs Connor

Reception have started the new term by celebrating the traditional festivities of Bonfire Night! We have been getting creative, making our own bonfire and firework pictures. The children have also loved building bonfires in the woods and, as the weather gets colder, we have enjoyed one of the best Bonfire Night traditions – gathering around the pretend bonfire in the woods, enjoying singing songs together. We have also been learning some important safety rules around bonfires and fireworks. The children have settled beautifully into their daily routines, and we couldn't be prouder of how well they are doing. What a fantastic start to the new term!
Kamkwamba Class have had a great week. Monday was our first Forest Schools session which was thoroughly enjoyed by all. On Wednesday, years 5 and 6 launched their new topic "Up, Up and Away". Activities included an egg drop challenge, making planes, spinners and rockets! All of the children showed great teamwork, enthusiasm and enjoyment throughout the day.

Maths at Bourton Primary:
At Bourton Primary, the EYFS children develop their mathematical understanding through investigating, exploring, talking, problem-solving and most importantly ‘doing’. In Reception, adults create a continuous learning environment that encourages children to notice, explore and apply mathematical ideas throughout their play and everyday experiences. Alongside this, carefully planned adult-led experiences provide opportunities to explicitly teach and develop key mathematical concepts, language and skills, building a strong foundation for future mathematical learning.
Throughout KS1 and KS2, our mathematics teaching builds upon the strong foundations developed in the EYFS. We incorporate a mastery approach, providing children with rich opportunities to develop conceptual understanding through practical experiences, carefully chosen resources and representations that are appropriately matched to their stage of learning. This enables children to develop fluency, reasoning and problem-solving skills, while building confidence and making connections between mathematical concepts.
Year 4 Multiplication tables check (MTC)
Having secure knowledge of times tables is crucial to children’s success in mathematics. Times tables are the building blocks for many areas of Maths and developing rapid recall helps children to access more complex mathematical concepts with greater confidence.
Here are some ways that secure times table knowledge benefits your child:
What is the Year 4 Multiplication check?
The Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check (MTC) is an annual statutory check in England that assesses children’s fluency in recalling multiplication facts. Children are expected to know their multiplication and division facts up to 12 × 12 by the end of Year 4, in line with the National Curriculum. The DfE introduced the check as part of its focus on developing secure numeracy skills and ensuring children have the mathematical knowledge they need for secondary school and beyond. The purpose of the MTC is to assess whether Year 4 pupils can recall their multiplication tables fluently, accurately and quickly, without needing to work out each answer. The pupils results will be included in their end of year report.
Multiplication Tables Check: Information for Parents/Carers
How can I help my child prepare for the MTC?
Times tables are best learnt through regular, short bursts of practice. At Bourton on-the-water Academy, we use Times Tables Rock Stars (TTRS) to support children in developing secure multiplication and division facts. The interactive platform makes practising times tables fun and engaging, allowing children to challenge themselves and compete against their friends and teachers.
The ‘Sound Check’ area has been specifically designed to help children prepare for the Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check and develop their fluency and speed.
Please click the link below to access the Times Tables Rock Stars pupil login area:
Numbots
Numbots and Times Table Rock Stars (TTRs) are regular homework tasks that will allow children to develop automaticity around counting, number facts and the times tables.
Numbots
NumBots is an online game. Playing little and often will significantly improve your child’s recall and understanding of number bonds, as well as addition and subtraction facts. These skills form critical foundations in mathematics.
Game Types
Story Mode This mode focuses on learning the ideas and concepts behind addition and subtraction. It includes more diagrams, shapes, and varied question styles.
Challenge Mode This mode focuses on the speed of recall of key facts, such as number bonds to 10, doubling small numbers, and adding or subtracting mentally.
Children are given logins from Reception. The programme is predominantly used in Years 1 and 2, although it can be accessed from Reception to Year 6.
Children in Reception to Years 2 will receive certificates, which are presented during Friday’s Start of the week Assemblies. Certificates are awarded for completed levels.
To play, log on to numbots.com or download the app.
For more information, please refer to the parent guide below.
Times Table Rock Stars (TTRs)
Times table Rock Stars
When it comes to times tables, speed and accuracy are essential. Times Table Rock Stars (TTRS) is a fun and challenging programme designed to help children master their times tables.
Times tables are explicitly taught in school and children are encouraged to practise at home using a range of methods, including games, songs, chants and TTRS.
All children from Year 2 (Spring term onwards) are given a login for the website by their class teacher. If your child has difficulty logging in, please speak to their class teacher.
Children in Years 3, 4, 5, and 6 can compete to win weekly certificates, which are presented during Friday’s Star of the week Assemblies. Certificates are awarded for change in Rock status and Gone Green.
Game Types
This is the only game mode without a timer, players chose the table and operation they want to practise.
Gigs last 5 minutes and contain up to 100 questions, which come in 'waves', starting with 10s, then 2s, 5s, 3s, 4s, 8s, 6s, 7s, 9s, 11s and 12s. These are to be completed once a month in school.
Players are given a personalised set of 6 multiplication questions in each round. This is probably the best game made for improving their recall while still learning.
Here players earn their Rock Status, which is based on their studio speed, this is based on an average of their most recent 10 studio games.
This game is the most like the Year 4 Multiplication Check (MTC), it gives players 25 questions, allowing 6 second for each question.
In Year 4, children complete the National Multiplication Check (MTC). This involves answering 25 multiplication questions, up to 12 × 12. Children have 6 seconds to answer each question. The results are reported to the Department for Education. However, there is no pass mark for the children.
To play, visit ttrockstars.com or download the app.
For more information, please refer to the parent guide below.

Reading at Bourton Primary:
At Bourton Primary, we believe reading is an essential life-long skill. We teach reading so that our pupils can read with fluency, accuracy and understanding. We want our pupils to develop a love of reading and encourage them to read for pleasure.
RWI Phonics:
Phonics is the key to unlocking reading and writing. At Bourton Primary we follow the RWI Phonics scheme. From the summer term in preschool, our children are exposed to the nursery programme of RWI.
Once children enter Reception, they begin learning their set 1 sounds in full and progress through the scheme until they reach the grey reading book assessment.
Here is a link to Read Write Inc Phonics - the Department of Education approved scheme we follow.
Reading for Pleasure:
As a school, we aim to inspire more children to read for pleasure. We do this through a number of avenues, including: our protected story time at 3pm for every class, every day, development of our outdoor reading area and creative reading areas in every classroom.
Reading at home is an excellent opportunity to help inspire and build a love of reading.
